templates.scenario: You are scheduled to open {workplace|the} tomorrow at 7:00. Tonight you find out your usual ride is not available. A coworker said they might be able to swap shifts with you, but nothing is confirmed.
templates.prompt: What is the most appropriate action?

options.text: Tell your {lead} tonight, share what you are doing to find a ride, and confirm any swap before the shift.
options.why: Early notice gives your {lead} time to plan, and showing you are working on a solution demonstrates that people can count on you.

options.text: Wait to see how the morning goes, then let your {lead} know as soon as you find out that you cannot get there.
options.why: Telling someone at the last minute leaves no time to arrange coverage for a shift that must be opened on time.
options.misconception: I only need to speak up if the problem actually happens.

options.text: Text the coworker to cover and assume the swap will work out without telling anyone else.
options.why: An unconfirmed swap is not coverage, and the person responsible for the schedule does not know. If it falls through, no one is prepared.
options.misconception: A casual maybe from a coworker counts as arranged.

options.text: Plan to arrive late if you must, since a few minutes will not matter for opening.
options.why: Opening has a set time because others depend on it. Planning to be late without warning shifts the problem onto coworkers.

templates.principle: Being dependable means giving early notice when a plan falls through and working to solve the problem, not leaving others to discover it.

templates.scenario: You work as {role|a} at {workplace|a}. Five minutes before you clock out, you realize you forgot to finish {task|the} that {coworker} is expecting to find done when the next shift starts. {coworker} is walking in now, and your {lead} has already left.

options.text: Tell {coworker} right now what is left on {task|the}, and finish what you can in the time you have.
options.why: Letting the next person know immediately means they can plan around the gap, and using your remaining minutes shows you are taking responsibility for it.

options.text: Clock out on time and let the next shift find out what was not finished.
options.why: Leaving without a word makes the next person discover the gap on their own and may delay work that depends on it.
options.misconception: My responsibility ends when my shift does.

options.text: Mark {task|the} as complete so it looks done, and plan to finish it tomorrow morning when you are back.
options.why: Marking unfinished work as complete makes the record untrue and leaves the next person depending on something that is not done.
options.misconception: Marking it done is fine if I finish it later.

options.text: Write a note blaming how busy the day was, and leave it by {task|the}.
options.why: A note full of excuses explains but does not help. The next person needs to know what is left, not why.
options.misconception: Explaining why is the same as taking responsibility.

templates.principle: Be accountable for your commitments: tell the next person what remains right away and use the time you have left to reduce the gap.

review.notes: Timing is explicit (five minutes, coworker arriving).

templates.timing: The coworker is arriving now, so informing them comes before anything else.

templates.scenario: At {workplace|the}, a mistake with {document|a} cost your team an hour of rework. You made the main error, though {coworker} also missed a chance to catch it. Your {lead} asks what happened.

options.text: Explain what you did, own your part in the error, and say how you will avoid it next time.
options.why: Owning your part plainly and offering a way to prevent it shows accountability and helps your lead fix the process.

options.text: Explain what happened, but also point out that {coworker} missed a chance to catch the error too, since it was a shared task.
options.why: It is fair to describe the whole picture, but leading with someone else's miss shifts attention from your own responsibility.
options.misconception: Sharing the blame reduces my share of it.

options.text: Say you are not sure what happened, to avoid guessing wrongly.
options.why: You know what you did. Claiming not to know avoids responsibility and gives your lead nothing to work with.
options.misconception: Saying less keeps me out of trouble.

options.text: Describe how busy the day was and how many things you were handling at once.
options.why: Context can be useful, but offered as the main answer it sounds like an excuse and does not address what to change.
options.misconception: A good explanation of the pressure should be enough.

templates.principle: Own your decisions and their consequences: describe what you did, take responsibility for your part, and propose a way to prevent a repeat.

review.notes: Acceptable option is honest but deflects; no legal claims.

templates.scenario: At {workplace|the}, your {lead} gives you a long job that will take most of the day.
templates.prompt: Arrange these steps in the order that best gets the job done well.

steps.text: Break the job into smaller parts
Work through each part until it is finished
Check the finished work against the instructions
Let your {lead} know the job is complete

precedence.why: Smaller parts make a long job manageable and keep you moving.
You can only check work that has been completed.
Reporting before checking risks telling your lead it is done when it is not.

templates.principle: Persistence means breaking large work into parts, finishing it, checking it, and then reporting it as done.

templates.scenario: A coworker at {workplace|the} leaves this note for the evening shift.
templates.prompt: Tap the line that is a problem.
templates.docTitle: Handoff note for the evening shift

segments.text: The morning tasks are all finished.
I did not get to the supply count, but I marked it complete so nobody worries.
segments.why: Marking an unfinished task complete misleads the next shift, who will rely on it being done.

segments.whyFine: A useful piece of information for the next shift.

segments.text: Call me if anything here is unclear.

templates.principle: Hand off work honestly: say what is not finished so the next person can plan around it.
